pr_title: fix(ivy): include type parameter for `ngBaseDef` declaration
pr_body:
When a class uses Angular decorators such as `@Input`, `@Output` and
friends without an Angular class decorator, they are compiled into a
static `ngBaseDef` field on the class, with the TypeScript declaration
of the class being altered to declare the `ngBaseDef` field to be of type
`ɵɵBaseDef`. This type however requires a generic type parameter that
corresponds with the type of the class, however the compiler did not
provide this type parameter. As a result, compiling a program where such
invalid `ngBaseDef` declarations are present will result in compilation
errors.

This commit fixes the problem by providing the generic type parameter.

Fixes #31160

@benelliott we are aware of that issue, it's a slight variation of the one reported here. A compilation error occurs for base classes without `@Directive()` decorator that require generic type arguments themselves.

You can probably workaround that issue by adding the `@Directive()` decorator to the base class, which ensures that an `ngDirectiveDef` is produced instead of the `ngBaseDef`; the former does not suffer from the same bug.

Your point regarding backwards compatibility is a valid concern for which I don't know the answer. I suspect it may indeed break, as you're afraid of.

As an alternative, you could insert a default type for the generic type parameter:

export class BaseComp<T> {}

becomes
